feedback: If the child points to the side of the globe for a pole, cue 'North = top, South = bottom' with an up/down gesture and have them point again.
If a child confuses the two poles, anchor North to the top and South to the bottom and practise pointing to each in turn.
Praise using the globe to turn and locate, not just naming from memory.
activities.intendedInsight: The poles are the top and bottom points of the Earth, and the Equator is the warm belt around the middle — a single spatial frame, not three unrelated facts.
learnerActions: Hold and turn a real globe or ball; point to the very top and say 'North Pole', then the very bottom and say 'South Pole'.
Run a finger around the middle band (the Equator) and say 'warm here'.
Say the simple rule out loud: 'middle is hot, top and bottom are cold.'
activities.title: Find the poles on a turnable globe

feedback: If a child says the poles are warm, use a globe coloured from a red-hot Equator to icy-blue caps so the hot stripe and cold ends are visible.

If a child says the poles are cold because the top of the Earth is closest to the Sun or to cold space, note that the whole Earth is roughly the same distance from the Sun; the poles are cold because the Sun's warmth is weakest at the top and bottom, furthest from the warm middle where it is strongest.
If a child locates the poles and knows they are cold but can't say why, re-trace the 'how far from the middle?' arrow and ask again.
activities.intendedInsight: The poles are so cold because the Sun's warmth is weakest at the top and bottom of the Earth, as far as possible from the Equator, where it is strongest. They are not random cold spots, and they are not cold because of being nearer to or further from the Sun.
learnerActions: With a finger on the warm Equator, trace an arrow outward to a pole and say the pole is the furthest place from the warm middle.
Answer: 'Are the poles the hottest or the coldest places on Earth?' and explain why in your own words.
Move a finger from the North Pole down towards the Equator and say whether it gets warmer or colder along the way.
activities.title: Why are the poles so cold?
